_readme: Test vectors for the GPS hackathon site. Generated by make_vectors.py from gps_sim.py. All lengths in metres. Earth is a sphere of radius 6371000 m, satellites on a sphere of radius 26560000 m, receiver at lat 37.5, lon 127.0, height 0, true receiver clock error 0.5 ms (cdt = c*0.0005). Solver: Gauss-Newton from the Earth centre with clock 0, 10 iterations.

kalman.description: Walker east at 1.4 m/s for 60 s then north for 60 s, 1 fix/s, noise 5 m per axis (numpy seed 11). Filter state [x,y,vx,vy], F=[[1,0,1,0],[0,1,0,1],[0,0,1,0],[0,0,0,1]], H picks x,y, Q=q^2*[[1/4,0,1/2,0],[0,1/4,0,1/2],[1/2,0,1,0],[0,1/2,0,1]], R=25*I, x0=[z0x,z0y,0,0], P0=diag(25,25,100,100). Predict then update for every fix including the first.

error_budget.source: National Academies 1995 Table 3-1 / 3-3, SPS, 1 sigma metres

klobuchar_demo.warning: alpha/beta are ILLUSTRATIVE values recalled from a documentation example, NOT verified against a source and not live broadcast values.

multipath.model: coherent early-late discriminator, triangular BPSK autocorrelation, reflection amplitude 0.5, worst-case (destructive) phase; error is zero beyond (1+spacing/2) chips
